unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 4: Payment and Settlement Systems Act — Distinguish payment systems, instructions, obligations, operators, participants and systemic risk

facts.statement: Courseware defines bank, derivative, electronic funds transfer, gross settlement, LEI/issuer, netting, instruction, obligation, system, settlement, participant and trade repository.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 178–179; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: A payment system enables payer-to-beneficiary payment involving clearing, payment or settlement services and excludes a stock exchange in its definition. Instruction is the payment order; obligation is inter-participant indebtedness from the specified processes; settlement discharges the relevant instructions. System participant includes the provider, which operates an authorised system. Systemic risk involves disruption/default transmission and likely system-stability impact. Derivative, LEI/issuer and trade-repository definitions address distinct functions.

payload.title: Read the instruction, the obligation and the service separately
payload.core_explanation_md:
A customer's **payment instruction** is an order or authorisation to effect payment. It can generate a **payment obligation** between system participants through clearing or settlement. **Settlement** addresses the payment instructions and can involve funds, securities, foreign exchange or derivatives. Treating these as synonyms makes it hard to see what has actually happened in a payment file.

The **payment system** supplies clearing, payment or settlement services between payer and beneficiary; it need not perform all three services to fit the definition. The definition excludes a stock exchange. A service's commercial name or digital appearance alone does not determine its classification.

self_check.prompt_text: Does receipt of an instruction prove that the resulting obligation has already been settled?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Instruction, obligation and settlement describe different parts of the process.

payload.title: An operator is also included among participants
payload.core_explanation_md:
A **system provider** operates an authorised payment system. A **system participant** can be a bank or another participating person and includes the provider. The provider and participant labels therefore are not mutually exclusive.

When investigating disruption, identify each role and its actual obligations. **Systemic risk** goes beyond an isolated inconvenience: one participant's inability to pay or a disruption may prevent others from meeting their obligations and threaten system stability. The definition focuses on the transmission and stability consequences, rather than the number of customer complaints alone.

self_check.prompt_text: Why can the same entity appear under both provider and participant labels?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The participant definition expressly includes the system provider.

payload.title: Separate valuation, identification and recordkeeping functions
payload.core_explanation_md:
A **derivative** derives its value from the specified underlying changes and is settled at a future date. A **legal entity identifier** identifies a person for the specified transactions; the **issuer** supplies that identifier. A **trade repository** handles electronic transaction records or data through functions such as collection, storage and dissemination.

These functions should not be conflated. Recording a derivative transaction is different from operating its settlement or bearing its payment obligation. Nor does an identifier itself authorise a provider to operate a payment system. Start with the activity actually carried out, then inspect the applicable legal requirements.

self_check.prompt_text: Does issuing an LEI by itself establish authorisation to operate a payment system?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Identification and payment-system operation are different functions with their own requirements.

payload.stem_md: A bank receives a customer instruction and immediately records every resulting inter-participant obligation as settled, without checking the settlement process. Which distinction has it lost?

options.text_md: An electronic instruction can never be a payment instruction
options.explanation_md: The definition expressly includes instructions in electronic form.

options.text_md: Only physical cash can create payment obligations
options.explanation_md: Payment obligations can arise from the specified clearing and settlement processes beyond cash.

options.text_md: An instruction, the resulting obligation and its settlement are separate events
options.explanation_md: Receipt of the order alone does not establish completion of the settlement process.

options.text_md: Every instruction automatically makes the customer a system provider
options.explanation_md: Giving an instruction does not make the customer the operator of an authorised payment system.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Receipt of the order alone does not establish completion of the settlement process.

payload.stem_md: A policy classifies providers and participants as entirely disjoint groups. What statutory definition requires correction of that policy?

options.text_md: System participant includes the system provider
options.explanation_md: The definition expressly includes the operator, so the groups are not necessarily disjoint.

options.text_md: Only customers can ever be participants
options.explanation_md: A participant can be a bank or another participating person and includes the provider.

options.text_md: A provider is excluded from participation because it operates rather than uses the system
options.explanation_md: The participant definition expressly includes the provider; operating the system does not create that exclusion.

options.text_md: The participant definition excludes every non-bank entity
options.explanation_md: A participant may be a bank or another participating person; the definition is not confined to banks.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The definition expressly includes the operator, so the groups are not necessarily disjoint.

payload.stem_md: A participant's failure to meet its obligations is likely to prevent several others from paying when due and affect system stability. Which feature distinguishes this from a complaint about one slow screen?

options.text_md: The incident has no likely effect on other participants ability to meet obligations
options.explanation_md: The stated propagation to other participants and system stability directly contradicts this isolated-impact description.

options.text_md: Only the original transaction value matters, regardless of inter-participant effects
options.explanation_md: Systemic risk turns on the specified propagation and stability consequences, not transaction size alone.

options.text_md: Only reputational risk can exist until a final monetary loss is measured
options.explanation_md: The statutory definition includes likely disruption and inability to pay; a realised final loss figure is not necessary for systemic-risk analysis.

options.text_md: The inability to pay can transmit to other participants and threaten stability
options.explanation_md: That propagation and likely stability impact is central to the systemic-risk definition.

payload.correct_explanation_md: That propagation and likely stability impact is central to the systemic-risk definition.
